item.read:
Two forced reads, both from the dock's endpoint measure (useDockExpandedSize). They sit inside the /speedtest point-mount long task: in trace-st1 that is the third task over 50 ms, starting at t 421-481 and lasting 82-89 ms in the five slow visits. The chunk is deploy-lt assets/index-C-91Qc5b.js, line 4. dist-u2's index-CAfpKQ-L.js has the same offsets. trace.mjs prints V8's 1-based line:column, and col-1 lands exactly on each token.

(1) The getter, 12.7-14.7 ms (UpdateLayoutTree 6.4-6.9 + Layout 6.3-7.8).
- Stack: `index tC 4:105979` < `setup 4:118514` < `cs 2:21865` < `v0 2:68377` < `g0 2:68166`. On cand the names are kC, E0 and S0.
- 105979 is the `.ready` in `R&&R.ready.then(()=>!y&&w())`. 118514 is GlassDock's setup call `tC({rootEl:l,contentEl:c,expandedEl:u,collapsedEl:f,axis:s})`.
- Once the set's ready promise has resolved, Blink's FontFaceSetDocument::ready() updates style and layout before it returns the promise.

(2) The resolved promise's callback, 11.6-12.7 ms, about 40 ms later in the same task. It runs at the microtask checkpoint after Vue's flush has inserted the dock.
- getSize: `Gt 4:102517` < `w 4:104154` < `(anon) 4:105998`, 8.2-9.8 ms (UpdateLayoutTree 7.1-8.9 + Layout 0.6-1.1). 102517 is getSize's `offsetWidth` branch, because the dock is horizontal: atlas's 'offsetHeight' is offsetWidth here. 104154 is capture's first getSize(root). 105998 is the `.then` callback.
- restSize under withOverrides: `Gt` < `a 4:103082` < `(anon) 4:103276` < `jo 4:102722` < `gd 4:103113`, 2.3-2.9 ms.
- keepScroll's scroll read: `md 4:102897` < `w 4:104286`, 0.6-1.0 ms.

No atlas or Vue frame forces layout in this task; Vue's frames appear only as callers. One neighbour is left out of the count: glass's motionTempo read (`Jf 4:43446`, getComputedStyle of --motion-tempo, called from an atlas route's spring setup). It costs 1.6-2.5 ms of style recalc, with no layout, on all six visits including the fast one.

The chunk's glass is a U-line build stamped 10.1.2, not the tag. It matches u/sp-integ-glass 8b4d8f82b: getSize at dockMorphMeasure.ts:11-15, attach's `if (!observer) capture()` at :417, fonts.ready at :428, the caller at GlassDock.vue:213.

On tag v10.1.2:
- src/components/dock/composables/dockMorphMeasure.ts:5-9 is getSize (:8 is `axis === "vertical" ? el.offsetHeight : el.offsetWidth`).
- capture starts at :152, and its first read is at :161.
- attach captures synchronously at :232.
- :242-243 is the fonts subscription.
- It is called during setup from src/components/dock/GlassDock.vue:200.

11.0.0's 5dd981dd7 (in v11.0.0, not in v10.1.2) moved attach's capture onto the ResizeObserver's first delivery.
item.on_master:
Present and unchanged. master's dockMorphMeasure.ts is byte-identical to v11.1.0.
- GlassDock.vue:212 calls `useDockExpandedSize({...})` during setup.
- dockMorphMeasure.ts:542-543 holds `const fonts = ... document.fonts` and `if (fonts) void fonts.ready.then(() => !disposed && capture())`, and :197's comment says 'and once fonts are ready'.
- capture is at :229. Its first read, at :244, is `getSize(root, a)`, and getSize is at :7-10.

So on master the two in-task reads are what is left: the getter at setup, and the callback's capture after mount. Master's capture writes only the endpoint vars and publishYield's data-run-fits and --dock-run-room-block. It starts no morph.
item.on_11_1_1: Present and unchanged. release/11.1.1 is identical to master for dockMorphMeasure.ts and GlassDock.vue (:542-543, called from GlassDock.vue:212). 11.1.1 is the exits patch and its list is frozen (scope header), so the cure does not go there.
item.cure:
ROOT. useDockExpandedSize subscribes to document.fonts.ready during GlassDock's setup (master dockMorphMeasure.ts:542-543). When the page's fonts have already loaded:
- Chromium's getter lays the page out in order to return the promise (12.7-14.7 ms).
- The resolved promise's callback then runs at the same task's microtask checkpoint, after Vue's flush has inserted the dock. Its capture() reads getSize(root), restSize under overrides and the run's scroll, which lays out the new subtree again (11.6-12.7 ms).

When the fonts are still loading, the getter forces nothing and the callback runs later, outside the task. That is the bimodality. Atlas's frame (4:102517) is the second half; the getter (4:105979) is the larger one.

SMALLEST CURE (11.1.2). Delete dockMorphMeasure.ts:542-543, and drop 'and once fonts are ready' from :197. Nothing loses a reading:
- Since 11.0.0 the first capture rides the observer's initial delivery, which comes after layout and before paint.
- A late font swap that moves a box the endpoint or the yield is read from resizes an observed box: the root, its parent, the layers, both panes, or any pane child except the run mark. That delivery captures again.
- A swap that changes only the hidden pane's natural size leaves --dock-expanded-px stale while the dock is at rest, where nothing reads it. The endpoints are read only under [data-morphing], and the morph's arm reads its own: an expand takes the root as laid out, and a collapse keeps the last expanded capture, which the root's entry keeps current.

This row needs no next-frame read and no borderBoxSize. useDockExpandedSize is internal, so no export, token or default changes. It is one commit, source and test. On merge it meets wi8's deletion of the file as a modify/delete conflict, resolved by keeping the deletion, so nothing is written twice.

One seat should build this with O-247 (1) (scope :56) and the RO-loop row (:134), because all three touch useDockExpandedSize.
- The RO-loop row will change the read in :477's delivery. Once the fonts callback is gone, that delivery is the only capture before first paint. Whatever it becomes, the first capture must still land before paint, for example in a requestAnimationFrame posted at attach. That callback runs before the first frame's layout, so the layout it forces is the frame's own and falls neither in the mount task nor in a delivery.
- Deferring the first capture to the frame after the first delivery is harmless for the endpoint vars. It is not harmless for data-run-fits and --dock-run-room-block, which run.css reads at rest (:403-429, :890-917) on a dock resting expanded with a run.

11.2.0 (wi8, ledger L-60). Take `sync("mount")` (useDockBody.ts:1328) out of the mount task and post it to a requestAnimationFrame registered in onMounted, ahead of the `shown` frame (:1329-1331). Do not move it into the ResizeObserver delivery:
- A layout read inside a delivery is what the RO-loop law forbids. In WebKit a read there gives a subtree whose stylesheet is still pending its boxes, and raises the loop error.
- `shown`'s rAF would run before that delivery anyway, so a second delivery in the same frame would travel from a box that never painted.

With the rAF:
- The read runs before that frame's layout, so the layout it forces is the one the frame runs anyway.
- The first value still goes through `if (!layout)` (:764) and is placed with no travel before first paint.
- `shown` still turns true after the read.
- The observer's first delivery finds the held boxes (heldSize) and reads nothing.

WITNESS (one Chromium cell per tree, per the scope's rule). Build a page that awaits document.fonts.ready, so the getter's resolved path is certain, then dynamically imports and mounts a collapsed horizontal GlassDock with a run of seats. Trace it with disabled-by-default-devtools.timeline.stack at 390 by touch, CPU 4x. Count the Layout/UpdateLayoutTree events inside the mount task whose source-mapped stack holds a dockMorphMeasure frame:
- RED on v11.1.0: the getter's pair plus the callback's getSize, restSize and scroll reads.
- GREEN on the 11.1.2 branch: 0.

For 11.2.0, run the same cell on wi8: no useDockBody frame should force layout in the mount task, and the WebKit stylesheet-hold run (audit/ro-loop/hold.sh) should raise no loop error from the dock.

MUST NOT CHANGE ON FIRST PAINT. Read these from a task posted in the first rAF; each must equal v11.1.0's:
- the dock's box and posture;
- --dock-collapsed-px and --dock-expanded-px on the root (read only under [data-morphing]);
- on a dock resting expanded with a run, data-run-fits and --dock-run-room-block;
- --dock-plate-cross-px (its own observer, untouched).

The first capture is placed with no transition, and on 11.1.x a capture never starts a morph. Later values behave as today: a FontFace that loads after mount and widens a seat label updates --dock-expanded-px through the observer, and an expand or collapse arms on the dock spring with endpoints read at its arm.

item.evidence:
trace-st1.json (speed-1/out), 3 visits per build, re-summed from the per-event rows:
- Slow visits (prod v0-v2, cand v0-v1): the glass dock's forced layout inside the mount task is 24.9 / 27.3 / 26.1 / 26.0 / 25.0 ms. That is the getter (12.68 / 14.66 / 14.09 / 13.51 / 13.38) plus the callback (12.2 / 12.7 / 12.1 / 12.5 / 11.6: getSize 8.2-9.8, restSize 2.3-2.9, scroll 0.6-1.0). The tasks run 84 / 89 / 83 / 82 / 82 ms.
- Fast visit (cand v2): the task runs 59 ms with no getter event. The callback's capture ran at t 528-532, after the task ended (510) and before the observer's delivery (536-540).
- Every visit: the observer's first-delivery capture (rooted at anon 4:105647, with the restSize frames just before it, whose stacks the probe cuts at five frames) runs outside the task and costs 2.8-4.5 ms. The only other forced work left in the task is motionTempo's 1.6-2.5 ms style recalc.

perfn-st2 (8 rounds): when the dock's layout is absent (forced 0-1 ms), the route-speedtest script still runs 49-73 ms, and only one of seven such visits falls under 50 ms. With the layout (25-32 ms) it runs 79-103 ms. So the cure takes about 25-30 ms of blocking off the mount, but the task stays a long task in most visits. Atlas's 'under 50 ms' does not follow from its own runs.

Column mapping: deploy-lt/assets/index-C-91Qc5b.js line 4 (served on 9283 per serve-9283.log). dist-u2/assets/index-CAfpKQ-L.js (9282) has identical offsets.

item.reply: Thanks for the trace. The layout comes from GlassDock subscribing to document.fonts.ready while it sets up: once the fonts have loaded, Chromium lays the page out just to return that promise, and the dock then measures again in the same task. 11.1.2 drops that subscription, and in 11.2.0 the redesigned dock takes its first measurement in the first frame instead of at mount; the dock's first frame looks the same in both. Your own runs show the point mount still taking about 50 to 73 ms without that layout, so expect roughly 25 ms less blocking rather than a task under 50 ms.

changed: read: the callback half was 11.0-13.6 ms; the trace gives 11.6-12.7 ms. Its getSize part is 8.2-9.8 ms, not 8.6-9.8, with UpdateLayoutTree at 7.1-8.9, not 7.7-8.9. The getter numbers and the task timings held.
read: v10.1.2 refs made exact (getSize :5-9, capture :152 with its first read at :161) and the U-line refs completed (getSize :11-15, attach :417).

read: added the one neighbour in the task, glass's motionTempo getComputedStyle (4:43446, 1.6-2.5 ms, style only, also on the fast visit), and confirmed that no atlas or Vue frame forces layout there.

dedupe_of: 'none' was wrong. O-215 (the dock's forced layout at first mount, carried into 11.2.0 by the wi8 ledger's L-60 above 16 ms) already owns the 11.2.0 half. Also explained why O-247 (1) does not cover /speedtest: that dock rests collapsed.

cure, 11.2.0: changed from 'do the first read in the ResizeObserver's first delivery' to 'post sync("mount") to a requestAnimationFrame registered in onMounted, ahead of the shown frame'. A layout read inside a delivery breaks the RO-loop law: in WebKit it gives a pending-stylesheet subtree its boxes and raises the loop error. Also, shown's rAF runs before that delivery, so a second delivery in the same frame could travel from a box that never painted.

cure, RO-loop interplay: 'deferring the dock's RO capture a frame is harmless' holds only for the endpoint vars. data-run-fits and --dock-run-room-block are read at rest by run.css, and once the fonts callback is gone the first delivery is their only writer before paint. So the shared seat must keep a first capture before paint (for example a rAF posted at attach). Also added O-247 (1) to that seat, since it touches the same call.

cure, safety argument: replaced 'the RO already covers any font swap' with the exact case. A swap in the hidden pane can leave the endpoint stale at rest, which is harmless because it is read only under [data-morphing] and the morph's arm reads its own.

cure, first-paint list: added data-run-fits, --dock-run-room-block and --dock-plate-cross-px. Removed 'the first capture starts no growing morph': on 11.1.x capture never starts a morph, and that growth morph exists only in atlas's U-line chunk. Restated 'later values' to match master.
cure, merge: 'merges up with no second writing' made exact. The merge is a modify/delete conflict, resolved by keeping wi8's deletion.

cure, witness: cut to one Chromium cell per tree, as the scope's witness rule requires. The RED count now names the getter's pair plus the callback's three reads, instead of 'two pairs'. Added the WebKit stylesheet-hold check for the 11.2.0 half.

on_dock_branch: a collapsed dock forces one layout in the mount task (fitRun returns early), and an open run whose fit flag changes is read twice. Tied it to the wi8 ledger's L-60 and to the law booked at W-0.8.md:252.

evidence: the observer delivery's out-of-task cost is 2.8-4.5 ms, not 1.1-1.5 ms, once the restSize frames whose stacks the probe cuts are counted. perfn-st2 shows the mount still runs 49-73 ms without the dock's layout, so atlas's 'under 50 ms' does not follow. HandMark.vue:497 noted for INBOUND.
reply: no longer implies the long task goes away (it is about 25 ms less blocking), and 11.2.0's first measurement is described as 'in the first frame' instead of 'from that observer'.
